Normalise homogeneous positions to the panel box

Source: R/scene-contract.R
normalise_homogeneous_3d.Rd

Homogeneous coordinates (x, y, z, w) with w > 0 stand for the point (x / w, y / w, z / w); with w = 0 they stand for the direction (x, y, z), a point at infinity. Rows with w < 0 are points of the far half of oriented projective space (Stolfi 1991): (x, y, z, w) and (-x, -y, -z, -w) are distinct, and only the half with w >= 0 after the camera pre map is drawn. This maps homogeneous positions in scale units to the homogeneous panel-box fractions that new_scene_packet() takes: each coordinate becomes (x - lo * w) / (hi - lo) and w is kept, so that positive multiples of a row give the same point and directions stay at infinity.

Usage

normalise_homogeneous_3d(x, y, z, w = 1, ranges)

Arguments

x, y, z

Homogeneous coordinates in scale units.

w

Homogeneous weight of either sign; 1 for ordinary points.

ranges

List with x, y and z, each the lower and upper limit of the panel range, as in panel_params$ranges.

Value

A list with x, y, z and w, the vertices of new_scene_packet().

Examples

normalise_homogeneous_3d(c(5, 1), c(0, 0), c(1, 0), w = c(1, 0),
  ranges = list(x = c(0, 10), y = c(-1, 1), z = c(0, 2)))
